children: Saudi Arabia's Almasane Alkobra Mining Company (AMAK) has reported 14 million tonnes of mineral resources at its Jabal Qaran project in the Najran region, following an independent mineral resource estimate (MRE).

The estimate, prepared by Cube Consulting in accordance with the JORC Code (2012), identified approximately 11.3 million tonnes of classified mineral resources and around 2.7 million tonnes of unclassified material, AMAK said in a stock exchange statement.

The classified resources comprise 9.7 million tonnes of polymetallic mineralisation grading 1.38 percent copper equivalent (CuEq) and 1.5 million tonnes of gold mineralisation grading an average 1.10 grams per tonne (g/t) of gold.
AMAK had announced in November 2025 the discovery of potentially economically viable resources containing copper, zinc, gold and silver within one of its exploration licences in Najran.

The company said further exploration drilling will target extensions of the known mineralisation at greater depths and in surrounding areas, as well as other prospective zones within the broader mineralised belt with the objective of assessing the potential for further growth in mineral resources.
AMAK said it is also progressing development-stage studies aimed at converting the exploration licence into a mining licence.

title: Saudi Arabia's AMAK reports 14mln tonnes of mineral resources at Jabal Qaran
